in_text_mentions: noted (Figure 2(a)). The remainder of her physical examination results were unremarkable. Histologic examination of a 4 mm punch biopsy specimen taken from one of the papules revealed marked hyperkeratosis and keratotic plug in follicular infundibulum, spongiosis, lymphocyte exocytosis, and perivascular and periadnexal lymphocytic infiltration (Figure 3). The diagnosis of FFD was made by clinical and histopathological findings. She was prescribed topical tacrolimus ointment (0,1%) twice daily for 3 months. After 3 months, there was no change in lesions, and treatment was stopped (Figure 2(b)).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Wide clinical photo of torso showing flesh-colored peristernal papules in article titled Fox-Fordyce disease on the peristernal region: a rare and atypical case. Location is atypical for Fox-Fordyce. B: Close-up clinical photo clearly showing multiple flesh-colored monomorphic papules in peristernal region, matching caption and Fox-Fordyce diagnosis. Atypical location. C: Magnified/dermoscopic view of same peristernal skin showing follicular-based skin changes in context of captioned Fox-Fordyce flesh-colored papules and article diagnosis.
